sentences.text: This creature lived approximately 121 million years ago and possessed a skull measuring 182 mm in length. It featured an elongated snout with a distinct concave upper profile.
Fossil evidence reveals traces of hair-like pycnofibres, which are fine filaments, visible at the back of the skull and neck vertebrae.
The skull and lower jaws contained about fifty teeth in total, each possessing sharp points.
The longest neck vertebra was 4.1 times longer than it was wide, while the first phalanx of the wing finger was the longest bone and equal in length to the shinbone.
The genus was named by Lü Junchang, Ji Qiang, Wei Xuefang, and Liu Yongqing in 2012.
A second juvenile specimen was referred to the genus in 2016, and research indicated that the original holotype was actually a juvenile, not an adult.

Later analysis placed the genus in the family Ctenochasmatidae as the sister species of Pterofiltrus, a relationship now confirmed as the genus is part of Ctenochasmatidae and is a sister taxon to Pterofiltrus.
Gladocephaloideus lived during the Early Cretaceous period in what is now western Liaoning, China, with a time range estimated from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
